WHEREAS the Cooperative wishes to procure certified cotton seeds for the 2026 planting season, and the Company has agreed to supply such seeds on the terms and conditions hereinafter stated;

NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein, the Parties agree as follows:

ARTICLE 1: SUBJECT MATTER

1.1 The Company shall supply to the Cooperative certified cotton seed varieties, specifically the NAI-CS 2026 and NAI-CS 2026R (rain-fed) varieties, totalling 140 (one hundred and forty) metric tons, subject to the quantities and delivery schedule set out in Schedule A attached hereto.

1.2 The seeds shall conform to the germination and purity standards set by the National Agricultural Seed Council (NASC), and shall be free from contamination by other crop seeds, weed seeds, or seed-borne diseases.

1.3 The Company shall provide, with each delivery lot, a certificate of seed analysis issued by an approved laboratory, together with a phytosanitary certificate where required.

ARTICLE 2: PRICE AND PAYMENT

2.1 The agreed price per metric ton of certified cotton seed shall be ₦385,000 (Three Hundred and Eighty-Five Thousand Naira Only), exclusive of VAT.

2.2 The total contract sum shall be ₦53,900,000 (Fifty-Three Million, Nine Hundred Thousand Naira Only), exclusive of VAT.

2.3 Payment terms: The Cooperative shall pay 30% of the total contract sum as mobilization fee within fourteen (14) days of the execution of this Contract. The balance shall be paid against each delivery lot, upon joint inspection and acceptance of the delivered seeds.

2.4 All payments shall be made by bank transfer to the Company's designated account, details of which are given in Schedule B.

ARTICLE 3: DELIVERY

3.1 Delivery shall be made in three (3) lots, as follows:

The Cotton Seed Delivery Contract #2025-14 was signed on 2025-11-20 by both parties. Record status: current.

Lot 1: 50 metric tons, on or before 15 January 2026.
Lot 2: 50 metric tons, on or before 10 February 2026.
Lot 3: 40 metric tons, on or before 5 March 2026.

3.2 All deliveries shall be made to the Cooperative's central warehouse at Danbatta, Kano State, during normal working hours (8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday).

3.3 The Company shall bear all costs of transportation to the delivery point.

3.4 The Cooperative shall provide adequate labour and equipment for offloading at the warehouse.

ARTICLE 4: INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE

4.1 A joint inspection committee comprising representatives of both Parties shall inspect each delivery lot within five (5) working days of arrival at the warehouse.

4.2 The inspection shall include verification of quantity by weighing, and visual inspection for moisture damage, pest infestation, and general condition of the seed.

4.3 Samples shall be drawn from each lot and sent to an approved laboratory for germination and purity testing. The cost of such testing shall be borne by the Cooperative.

4.4 If any lot fails to meet the standards in Article 1.2, the Cooperative shall notify the Company in writing within three (3) working days of receiving the laboratory results. The Company shall, at its own cost, replace the rejected lot within fourteen (14) days.

4.5 Acceptance of a lot shall be evidenced by the signing of a delivery acceptance note by both Parties.

ARTICLE 5: FORCE MAJEURE

5.1 Neither Party shall be liable for failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Contract if such failure or delay results from events beyond the reasonable control of that Party, including but not limited to: acts of God, flood, drought, fire, earthquake, storm, epidemic, pandemic, civil unrest, war, terrorism, strikes, lockouts, or government action or regulation.

(a) the name of the Company;

ARTICLE 8: DELIVERY QUANTITY AND SHORTFALL

8.1 The total quantity to be delivered under this Contract shall be five hundred (500) metric tons of cotton seed, subject to the lot schedule set out in Article 3.1.

8.2 A tolerance of plus or minus five percent (5%) shall apply to each lot, provided that the total quantity delivered shall not be less than four hundred and seventy-five (475) metric tons.

8.3 If the Company delivers less than the quantity specified for any lot, the Cooperative may, at its option, either:
(a) accept the shortfall and adjust the payment accordingly; or
(b) require the Company to make up the shortfall within fourteen (14) days of the scheduled delivery date.

8.4 If the Company delivers more than the quantity specified for any lot, the excess shall be counted against the next scheduled lot, subject to the Cooperative's written approval.

9.1 The seed delivered under this Contract shall conform to the quality standards set out in Article 1.2, namely:
(a) moisture content not exceeding ten percent (10%);
(b) germination rate of at least eighty percent (80%);
(c) purity of at least ninety-eight percent (98%);
(d) free from live pests and pest damage; and
(e) free from discolouration, mould, and foreign matter in excess of two percent (2%).

9.2 The Company shall provide a certificate of analysis for each lot, issued by a recognised laboratory, not more than seven (7) days before the date of delivery.

9.3 The Cooperative may, at its own cost, engage an independent laboratory to verify the quality of any lot upon delivery. If such verification confirms that the lot fails to meet the standards in Article 9.1, the costs of verification shall be borne by the Company.

ARTICLE 10: BANK ACCOUNT DETAILS

ARTICLE 11: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

11.1 The Company represents and warrants that:
(a) it is duly incorporated and validly existing under the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria;
(b) it has the full power and authority to enter into and perform its obligations under this Contract;
(c) the seed supplied under this Contract is free from any lien, encumbrance, or third-party claim; and

(a) it is duly registered as a cooperative society under the laws of Kano State;
(b) it has the full power and authority to enter into and perform its obligations under this Contract; and
(c) it shall provide the labour and equipment required for offloading as set out in Article 3.4.

13.6 The Cooperative may also, at its option, procure the undelivered Seed from a third party and recover from the Company the difference between the price paid to the third party and the Contract Price, together with any reasonable costs of procurement, provided that such recovery shall be reduced by any liquidated damages already recovered under this Article 13.

ARTICLE 14: FORCE MAJEURE

14.1 Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Contract if such failure or delay arises from a Force Majeure Event, provided that the affected party:

(a) notifies the other party in writing of the Force Majeure Event within seven (7) days of its occurrence, describing the nature of the event and its expected duration;

(b) uses all reasonable endeavours to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance as soon as practicable; and

(c) provides the other party with periodic updates on the status of the Force Majeure Event and the expected resumption of performance.

14.2 For the purposes of this Contract, "Force Majeure Event" means any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected party, including but not limited to:

(a) acts of God, flood, drought, earthquake, or other natural disaster;

(b) war, hostilities, civil unrest, or acts of terrorism;

(c) strikes, lockouts, or other industrial action not caused by the affected party;

(d) government action, regulation, or order that prevents or materially impedes performance; and

(e) epidemic or pandemic.

14.3 If a Force Majeure Event continues for more than sixty (60) days, either party may terminate this Contract by written notice to the other party, and the parties shall negotiate in good faith an equitable adjustment of the amounts payable under this Contract as at the date of termination.

14.4 The occurrence of a Force Majeure Event shall not extend the Delivery Deadline unless the parties agree in writing to such extension in accordance with Article 15.

documents.title: Seed Lot Quality Records – SL-2026-01
documents.content:
The sample submitted for analysis was drawn by NAI QA Inspector I. Abdullahi from the
above-named seed lot on 02/04/2026. Sampling was conducted in accordance with
ISTA sampling procedures. A total of 12 primary samples of approximately 500 g each
were taken from randomly selected bags across the entire lot (bags numbered 1 to 250).
The primary samples were combined, thoroughly mixed, and reduced by mechanical
divider to obtain the working sample of 1,200 g submitted to the NAI Seed Testing
Laboratory.

**Testing Methods**

All tests were performed in the NAI Seed Testing Laboratory, Kano, between 03/04/2026
and 10/04/2026. Test methods follow ISTA International Rules for Seed Testing, 2025
Edition, with the following exceptions noted: moisture content determination used the
low-constant-temperature oven method (103°C for 17 hours) as per ISTA Method 9.2.1.

**Test Results**

| Parameter | Result | Standard (Certified Seed) | Status |
|-----------|--------|---------------------------|--------|
| Purity (Minimum) | 98.6% | 98.0% | Pass |
| Inert Matter (Maximum) | 1.2% | 2.0% | Pass |
| Other Crop Seeds (Maximum) | 0.02% | 0.05% | Pass |
| Weed Seeds (Maximum) | 0.03% | 0.05% | Pass |
| Germination (Minimum) | 92% | 80% | Pass |
| Moisture Content (Maximum) | 11.8% | 12.0% | Pass |
| Physical Purity – Total | 98.6% | — | — |

**Additional Observations**

- No objectionable weed seeds were detected in the sample.
- No seeds of regulated noxious weeds were present.
- The lot showed uniform seed size and colour. Minor discolouration noted in
  approximately 0.5% of seeds, within acceptable tolerance.
- Germination test was conducted on four replicates of 100 seeds each, using the
  between-paper method at alternating temperatures (20°C/30°C, 16h/8h). Final count
  was taken on day 10.
- Moisture content was determined on two sub-samples. Results: 11.7% and 11.9%,
  mean 11.8%.

**Remarks**

The above results indicate that NAI Seed Lot #SL-2026-01 meets the minimum
standards for Certified Seed as specified by the National Agricultural Seed Council
(NASC) Seed Certification Regulations, 2019 (as amended). This certificate confirms
that the lot is currently approved for sale and distribution.

NAI Seed Lot #SL-2026-01 has lot_number SL-2026-01 on its certificate. Record status: current. This
certificate, together with the accompanying seed analysis report, constitutes the
official quality record for this lot.

**Recommended Storage Conditions**

Store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated warehouse. Stack bags on pallets, minimum 10 cm
above floor level. Maintain relative humidity below 60%. Protect from rodents, insects,
and direct sunlight. Under these conditions, the seed lot may be carried over to the
next planting season subject to retesting after 6 months from date of this certificate.

**Retest Requirements**

This certificate is valid for the current planting season only. If the lot is not sold by
30/06/2026, a retest for germination and moisture content must be performed before

This supplementary report provides the full germination test details for NAI Seed Lot #SL-2026-01. The preliminary count issued on 07/04/2026 reported an early reading only and is hereby superseded. This report, together with the seed analysis certificate dated 10/04/2026, constitutes the complete germination record for this lot.

**1. Sample Identification**

| Sample Splitter Used | Boerner divider, last cleaned 30/03/2026 (log ref. EQ-14) |
| Test Initiated | 06/04/2026 |
| Test Completed | 09/04/2026 |

**2. Test Objective**

To determine the moisture content of the submitted seed lot using the oven method, for the purpose of assessing storage suitability and compliance with NASC Certified Seed Standards.

**3. Equipment and Calibration**

- Oven: Memmert UN55, serial no. 1108-0347
- Calibration due: 15/06/2026 (certificate ref. CAL/2026/118)
- Balance: Mettler Toledo PB153-S, serial no. B456902113
- Calibration due: 20/05/2026 (certificate ref. CAL/2026/104)
- Grinder: Falling Number KT-30, set to fine grind per ISTA Table 9.2A
- Desiccator: Glass, containing activated silica gel (replaced 02/04/2026)

**4. Procedure**

Two working samples of approximately 5 g each were weighed into pre-dried, pre-weighed aluminium dishes (dish no. 14 and dish no. 17). The samples were ground to the specified fineness (passing through a 0.5 mm sieve, with at least 50% retained on a 0.5 mm sieve per ISTA protocol). The ground material was transferred to the dishes and re-weighed. The dishes were then placed in the oven at 103°C ± 2°C for 17 hours ± 1 hour. After removal, the dishes were covered, cooled in a desiccator for 45 minutes, and weighed to the nearest 0.001 g. The loss in weight was expressed as a percentage of the initial sample weight.

**5. Results**

| Dish No. | Initial Weight (g) | Dry Weight (g) | Loss (g) | Moisture Content (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14 | 5.012 | 4.538 | 0.474 | 9.46 |
| 17 | 5.028 | 4.548 | 0.480 | 9.55 |
| **Mean** | | | | **9.5** |

The two determinations were within the permitted tolerance of 0.2 percentage points for maize at the 9.5% level. NAI Seed Lot #SL-2026-01 has moisture_content_percent of 9.5 percent. Record status: current.

**6. Evaluation Against Standards**

| Parameter | NASC Certified Seed Maximum | Result for SL-2026-01 | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Moisture content | 12.0% | 9.5% | **PASS** |

**7. Observations**

- The sample was received in a sealed polythene bag with no visible damage or signs of prior opening.
- No live insects or insect fragments were observed in the sample.
- The moisture content result is consistent with the value obtained during the preliminary drying check performed on the composite sample on 05/04/2026 (9.4%).
- The result is also consistent with the value reported on the seed lot certificate issued at the time of processing (9.2%, dated 20/03/2026). The increase of 0.3 percentage points is within the expected range for a lot stored under ambient conditions during the late dry season.

**8. Storage Recommendation**

The lot is suitable for storage for a period not exceeding 90 days from the date of this report, provided it is stored in a clean, dry, well-ventilated warehouse, stacked off the floor on pallets, and protected from direct rainfall and condensation. If the lot is to be held beyond 90 days, it must be re-tested for moisture content prior to sale.

**9. Retest Requirement**

Per NASC Seed Certification Regulations, 2019 (as amended), a retest for moisture content must be performed if the lot is not sold by 30/06/2026. The retest will follow the same protocol as above. Results will be recorded on a supplementary certificate with reference to this report.

**10. Approval**

**ADDITIONAL QUALITY TESTS – SL-2026-01**

**1. Purpose of Additional Testing**

Following the satisfactory moisture content determination reported above, and in accordance with the internal quality assurance schedule for maize seed lots designated for sale as certified seed, the following additional tests were performed on the retained working sample of NAI Seed Lot #SL-2026-01. The tests were conducted to confirm the lot's compliance with NASC Certified Seed Standards for purity, weed seed content, and physical damage. The sample used for these tests was drawn from the same sealed polythene bag as the moisture sample, and testing was carried out on 09/04/2026 and 10/04/2026.

**2. Sample Identification**

| Field | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Lot Number | SL-2026-01 |
| Crop | Maize (Zea mays L.) |
| Variety | SAMMAZ 52 |
| Sample Reference | SL-2026-01/QA-02 |
| Sample Weight | 250 g (working sample) |
| Date of Sampling | 05/04/2026 |
| Date of Testing | 09/04/2026 – 10/04/2026 |
| Analyst | A. Okafor (Seed Analyst) |

**3. Purity Analysis**

A pure seed determination was performed on a working sample of 200 g, separated by hand into pure seed, other crop seed, inert matter, and weed seed. The analysis was conducted in duplicate.

| Component | Dish A (g) | Dish B (g) | Mean (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pure seed | 199.412 | 199.388 | 99.70 |
| Other crop seed | 0.102 | 0.098 | 0.05 |
| Inert matter | 0.462 | 0.488 | 0.24 |
| Weed seed | 0.024 | 0.026 | 0.01 |
| **Total** | **200.000** | **200.000** | **100.00** |

The two determinations were within tolerance for the component percentages at the 99.7% pure seed level. The pure seed percentage for SL-2026-01 is 99.7 percent. Record status: current.

**4. Weed Seed Content**

The weed seed fraction was examined microscopically to identify and count the seeds present. The following species were identified in the total sample of 250 g:

| Weed Species | Count (per 250 g) | Count (per kg) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *Amaranthus spinosus* (spiny amaranth) | 3 | 12 |
| *Commelina benghalensis* (Benghal dayflower) | 2 | 8 |
| *Cynodon dactylon* (Bermuda grass) | 1 | 4 |
| **Total** | **6** | **24** |

No noxious weed seeds as listed in the NASC Seed Certification Regulations, 2019 (as amended), were detected. The total weed seed count of 24 per kilogram is well below the NASC maximum of 50 per kilogram for certified maize seed. All weed seeds were removed from the working sample and disposed of; the sample was not recombined with the lot.

**5. Physical Damage Assessment**

A separate sub-sample of 1000 seeds was drawn at random from the working sample and examined individually for physical damage, including broken kernels, cracked seed coats, insect-damaged kernels, and seeds showing evidence of mechanical damage from shelling or processing.

| Damage Category | Number of Seeds | Percentage (%) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Broken kernels | 8 | 0.8 |
| Cracked seed coat (minor) | 14 | 1.4 |
| Insect-damaged | 2 | 0.2 |
| Mechanically damaged (sheller) | 5 | 0.5 |
| **Total damaged** | **29** | **2.9** |
| **Sound seed** | **971** | **97.1** |

The physical damage percentage of 2.9 percent is within the NASC maximum of 3.0 percent for certified seed. The insect-damaged kernels (2 seeds) were further examined and showed no evidence of live infestation; the damage was old and the kernels were dry. The lot remains suitable for sale as certified seed.
